name: Wood-ash glazing of proto-porcelain at Deqing
summary: A study reconstructs deliberate application of lime-rich wood ash to Deqing proto-porcelain vessels to form a glaze during firing.
description: Yin interprets chemical analysis of proto-porcelain sherds from Deqing kiln sites as evidence that potters deliberately applied lime-rich wood ash to vessels, which reacted with the ceramic body during firing to form a glaze. The study lists 12 excavated Shang-period Nanshan sherds and presents glaze analyses for four (NS-1, NS-4, NS-8 and NS-11). The exact preparation of the ash is unresolved; this reconstruction does not establish that every proto-porcelain producer used this method.

date.label: Shang dynasty, c. 1700–1027 BCE
date.basis: Yin identifies the Nanshan samples as Shang in Table 3.1 and gives these broad dynasty bounds in the abstract.

events.statement: Yin interprets glaze chemistry of sampled Deqing proto-porcelain, including four analysed Shang-period Nanshan glazes, as evidence of deliberate application of lime-rich wood ash before firing.

evidence.locator: p. 3; pp. 73–75, Table 3.1; pp. 132–135 and 138–143; Appendix 3, Table A 3.1, p. 271
evidence.supports: Yin reconstructs deliberate application of lime-rich wood ash and its reaction with the body from the analysed Deqing sherds. Table 3.1 lists 12 excavated Nanshan sherds, while Table A 3.1 presents glaze analyses for NS-1, NS-4, NS-8 and NS-11; ash preparation remains unresolved.

earliest_record.rationale: The sampled Nanshan sherds are attributed to the Shang; the dynasty bounds do not resolve the date of the glazing process more narrowly or establish its first use.

unresolved.note: Was the ash washed, taken from the firebox after depletion of potash, or prepared another way? Yin discusses alternatives; do not infer one method.
How widely did the same glazing process apply outside the analysed Deqing production-site samples, and what were its origins?
